newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cartel body warns Lufthansa on fares.
newsitem.headline: German cartel body warns Lufthansa on fares.

text.p: Germany's Federal Cartel Office on Wednesday gave Deutsche Lufthansa AG an official warning over the fares it charges on the key Berlin-Frankfurt domestic route.
A spokeswoman for the cartel office said it would require the airline to reduce its fares on the route to equivalent journeys, and had given Lufthansa a month to make a response to the warning.
Lufthansa rejected the criticism and queried the legal standing of the office's warning to it.

"The warning itself has no legal effect of its own and comprises a number of legally disputed questions," the airline said in a statement from Frankfurt. It added it would seek a full legal clarification of the implications as soon as possible.
Lufthansa argues that the fares it charges on this route -- such as 840 marks return for Business Class -- do not fully cover its costs, and so cannot be viewed as excessive.
Lufthansa contends any fares lower than its own must by definition be even less commercially sustainable than its own.
